manifest.name: dsh-tinyfish-search
manifest.description: TinyFish-backed web search provider for DeepSeek Harness (ctx.web): makes the built-in web_search tool run on the TinyFish Search API

bundle.text:
# dsh-tinyfish-search bundle layer.
#
# Three rows:
#  1. `dsh-tinyfish-search` — this plugin: registers the `tinyfish` search
#     provider on the ctx.web seam. The row references the package by name so
#     Node resolution finds the installed code (npm, tarball, or git install).
#     Its `config` mapping is the documented scaffolding: every field is
#     optional and commented out, so the shipped defaults apply until a later
#     layer (profile / home cordis.patch.yml / --patch) overrides this row by id.
#  2. `web` — points ctx.web at this provider. The dsh-base bundle pins
#     `searchProvider: deepseek-official` on the `web` row, so merely
#     registering a provider would leave web_search on the DeepSeek backend
#     even with this bundle installed. Per the layer rules a bundle patch may
#     override an earlier row by id, restating every key the row needs (config
#     is replaced wholesale, never deep-merged). Later layers (profile / home
#     cordis.patch.yml / --patch overlays) can still override this row by id.
#  3. `tool-web` — re-enables the HOST-level model-facing web tools. The
#     dsh-web-app bundle ships `tool-web` disabled because the Web app composes
#     the tools per agent preset; dsh-base keeps it enabled. Restating the row
#     with `disabled: false` re-enables the tools at the host layer, so they
#     are visible to EVERY preset on profiles that compose this bundle —
#     including presets that would not otherwise carry web tools (e.g.
#     `minimal`). Per-preset web enablement is untouched: a preset that mounts
#     its own `tool-web` row shadows this global registration for its agents.
#     If you want the tools scoped to one preset instead, remove this row in
#     your profile's cordis.patch.yml and add `tool-web` to that preset's
#     agent composition. Restates every dsh-base key for the same
#     replace-wholesale reason as above.
#
# Users can override any of these in their profile's cordis.patch.yml — the
# user layer applies after bundle layers ("last write wins per row").

- insert:
    - id: dsh-tinyfish-search
      name: dsh-tinyfish-search
      config:
        # apiKey: "literal-key"          # alternative to the env var; avoid committing it
        # apiKeyEnv: TINYFISH_API_KEY     # default
        # baseURL: https://api.search.tinyfish.ai   # default
        # location: US                    # optional geo targeting forwarded to TinyFish
        # language: en                    # optional search language forwarded to TinyFish
- id: web
  config:
    searchProvider: tinyfish
    fetchProvider: http
- id: tool-web
  # `disabled: false` is REQUIRED: the merge is per-key, so a config-only row
  # would leave the `disabled: true` shipped by the dsh-web-app bundle in place
  # and web_search would never register.
  disabled: false
  config:
    search: true
    fetch: true
    searchTimeoutMs: 60000
    fetchTimeoutMs: 30000

readme.text:
> This project is maintained with the assistance of dsh-superagent.

English | [Chinese](https://github.com/maxwell-feng/dsh-tinyfish-search/blob/main/README.zh.md)

> [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin that backs the built-in `web_search` tool with the [TinyFish Search API](https://docs.tinyfish.ai/search-api). One GET per query, no model call — fast and free (TinyFish Search is free at any wallet balance).

DeepSeek Harness's built-in `web_search` tool normally runs through the DeepSeek Anthropic-compatible endpoint (`web-search-deepseek`). This plugin registers an alternative **web search provider** on the `ctx.web` capability seam:

- Stable provider id: `tinyfish`
- Every `web_search` call becomes `GET https://api.search.tinyfish.ai?query=...` with the `X-API-Key` header
- `results[]` (title / snippet / url / date) are normalized into the seam's portable source shape
- Reports provider readiness through `WebSearchProvider.ready()` (DeepSeek Harness 0.2.2+): the harness asks it before it declares `web_search`, so a profile with no usable TinyFish credential simply shows no `web_search` tool instead of a tool whose every call fails
- No LLM turn consumed per search — unlike the Anthropic server-tool approach
- Bundled native `icon.svg` vector artwork and bilingual manifest resources (`locale/en.json`, `locale/zh.json`) conforming to DSH 0.2.2-rc.1 display conventions for Plugin Manager
- Pure TypeScript architecture across sources, scripts, and build configurations

Installing the bundle **takes over the built-in `web_search` automatically**: the
bundle patch overrides the `web` seam row (`searchProvider: tinyfish`,
`fetchProvider: http` restated), because `dsh-base` pins the seam to
`deepseek-official` and would otherwise keep the tool on the DeepSeek backend.
It also **re-enables the host-level `tool-web` row** (`disabled: false` plus
`search: true`, `fetch: true` and the base timeouts restated): the
`dsh-web-app` bundle ships that row disabled (the Web app normally composes
web tools per agent preset), so without it the model would see no `web_search`
tool at all on a clean web profile install. **Scope note:** re-enabling the
host row makes the tools visible to *every* agent preset on the profile —
including presets that would not otherwise carry web tools (e.g. `minimal`);
a preset that mounts its own `tool-web` row still shadows this global
registration for its agents. To scope the tools to one preset instead,
override or remove the `tool-web` row in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml`
and add `tool-web` to that preset's agent composition. Later layers (profile
/ home `cordis.patch.yml` / `--patch`) can still override both rows.

Configuration is declared as a **volatile schema** (DeepSeek Harness 0.1.7+): the
Host reads the `Config` schema this plugin exports and renders it as the form for
the `dsh-tinyfish-search` row on the Plugins page. There is no plugin-side
settings registration and no plugin-supplied browser half. A saved edit reaches
the next search without a restart.

- DeepSeek Harness `dsh` CLI (any profile with the web seam, e.g. `web`) — the build baseline is `0.2.2-rc.1` (released 2026-11-04 on the npm `next` tag) and the plugin is also verified on `0.2.1-rc.5` (npm `latest`, the desktop runtime); `0.2.2` carries `WebSearchProvider.ready()` while the `0.2.1-rc.*` maintenance line predates it, so a profile on that line runs the plugin without the readiness gate; the plugin declares `engines.dsh` `>=0.1.7-alpha.2 <0.3.0`, so the whole `0.1.7` prerelease line and the `0.2.x` line are admitted
- Node.js `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0` (matches the harness engine range) — on a `0.2.2-rc.1` host the effective floor is Node 24.9, because that host raises its own minimum to 24.9 and refuses to run below it; this plugin's `engines.node` is unchanged
- A [TinyFish API key](https://agent.tinyfish.ai/api-keys) (free to create; Search is free)
- The harness credential seam and launch environment (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-credentials`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-launch-environment`) are required peers — every `dsh` profile carries them already

DeepSeek Harness verifies a plugin's declared runtime requirement against the
running runtime **before** it admits the row, and refuses an incompatible plugin
instead of loading it. **Since `0.2.1-alpha.4` the rule reads differently:** when
a package declares its own `engines.dsh` range, that range decides alone and the
`@deepseek-ai/dsh*` `peerDependencies` are ignored for the compatibility
judgement; the peers are consulted only as a fallback when `engines.dsh` is
absent. Both are matched with prerelease semantics
(`semver.satisfies(runtime, range, { includePrerelease: true })`), so prerelease
runtimes participate in the comparison, and a refusal record reports
`requirements` rather than `peers`.

This plugin declares `engines.dsh: ">=0.1.7-alpha.2 <0.3.0"`, and that range
holds on `0.2.2-rc.1`, on `0.2.1-rc.5`, on `0.2.0-rc.2`, on `0.2.0-rc.1`, and
on the whole `0.1.7` prerelease line — so no exemption is needed. Because
`0.14.0` and `0.13.0` already declared that widened range in `engines.dsh` as
well, they remain admitted on `0.2.2-rc.1` too. The narrow-range `0.12.0`,
however, declared `^0.1.7-alpha.2`, which excludes `0.2.x`, so the harness still
refuses `0.12.0` on `0.2.x`: upgrade to `0.19.0` instead of granting an
exemption. If you run a `dsh` outside the declared range, DSH refuses the row
with a diagnostic naming the exact requirement pair; to accept that risk
explicitly, grant the exempted exact pair it prints:

```sh
dsh plugin allow-version dsh-tinyfish-search@0.19.0 --dsh-version <your-dsh-version> --accept-risk
```

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-tinyfish-search
```

or from the repository / a tarball:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-tinyfish-search        # source checkout
dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-tinyfish-search-0.19.0.tgz
dsh plugin --profile web add github:maxwell-feng/dsh-tinyfish-search
```

> **CLI syntax note**: Per DeepSeek Harness 0.2.1-alpha.1 specifications, `--profile <name>` must always precede forwarded subcommands like `add`, `remove`, and `update`.
>
> Git installs fetch sources, not built artifacts: pnpm runs the package's `prepare` script, which compiles `lib/` from source via `tsc -p tsconfig.build.json`.

See the [Install Guide](INSTALL.md) for requirements, all install methods, and verification.

Set your API key (recommended — no secret in config files):

**Linux / macOS:**

```sh
export TINYFISH_API_KEY="your_api_key_here"                      # current shell
echo 'export TINYFISH_API_KEY="your_api_key_here"' >> ~/.bashrc  # permanent (bash)
echo 'export TINYFISH_API_KEY="your_api_key_here"' >> ~/.zshrc   # permanent (zsh)
source ~/.bashrc                                                 # or reopen the terminal

**Windows (PowerShell):**

```powershell
setx TINYFISH_API_KEY "your_api_key_here"    # permanent — takes effect in new terminals
$env:TINYFISH_API_KEY = "your_api_key_here"  # current session only
```

Or set fields in your profile's `cordis.yml` / patch layer:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: dsh-tinyfish-search
      name: dsh-tinyfish-search
      config:

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `apiKey` | — | Literal TinyFish API key (secret role; wins over the env var) |
| `apiKeyEnv` | `TINYFISH_API_KEY` | Environment variable carrying the API key |
| `baseURL` | `https://api.search.tinyfish.ai` | TinyFish Search API endpoint base |
| `location` | — | Optional geo location forwarded as TinyFish's `location` (e.g. `US`); blank/unset sends nothing |
| `language` | — | Optional search language forwarded as TinyFish's `language` (e.g. `en`); blank/unset sends nothing |
See the [Configuration Guide](CONFIG.md) for the full schema, credential resolution order, and runtime settings UI.

```sh
dsh --profile web --dump-config | grep tinyfish   # layer present
```

Inside a session, call `web_search` and check that results carry TinyFish URLs/snippets. The web search settings card in the GUI shows the provider state.

After installation, no code changes required. In any session with the `web` profile:

1. The model calls `web_search` as usual (e.g. "search for TinyFish docs").
2. The harness routes it through `ctx.web → tinyfish → https://api.search.tinyfish.ai`.
3. Results appear as `WebSearchSource[]` (`url` / `title` / `snippet` / `publishedAt`) in the tool result.
4. Check GUI: **Settings → Web Search** shows provider `tinyfish` and `available: true` when the API key is configured.

Availability, readiness and failure are three different signals. `available()` is a cheap local check the seam uses to pick a provider while an operation runs. `ready()` answers whether a search for a model request on a given chat route has a credential to send, and `dsh-tool-web` uses it as the activation condition of `web_search` — no usable credential, no tool. A search that still runs without a key (for example a programmatic caller that bypasses the gate) fails with `WEB_PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_MISSING` rather than reaching TinyFish unauthenticated.

Abort and error semantics follow the `dsh-web` seam: `WEB_PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_MISSING` when no key, `WEB_ABORTED` on cancellation, `WEB_PROVIDER_ERROR` otherwise.

TinyFish returns no long-form summary and no generated answer, so the plugin fills neither `WebSearchSource.summary` nor `WebSearchResult.content`: both are optional on the seam because not every provider returns them, and inventing a value would make the seam lie.
See the [Usage Guide](USAGE.md) for providers, credential configuration, worked examples, and the error table.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-tinyfish-search
```

Removes the bundle layer and the `tinyfish` provider registration, and restores
the composed `web` / `tool-web` rows to exactly what the underlying bundles
ship (an inserted row's override returns to the row's own defaults when the
inserting layer is removed). Restart `dsh --profile web` to confirm
`web_search` falls back to the base `deepseek-official` provider (or none if
no other provider is installed).

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-tinyfish-search@latest

The repository is TypeScript throughout; there is no JavaScript source to keep in
sync. The bilingual-documents gate is
[`scripts/check-docs-language.ts`](./scripts/check-docs-language.ts), which CI runs
with bare Node (no dependencies installed) before the install step:

```sh
node scripts/check-docs-language.ts
```

Publishing to npm runs through GitHub Actions with npm **Trusted Publishing** (OIDC) — see [`.github/workflows/publish.yml`](./.github/workflows/publish.yml) and the [npm docs](https://docs.npmjs.com/trusted-publishers/). Tag `vX.Y.Z` (or dispatch the workflow) to release; provenance is generated automatically.
See [CHANGELOG.md](./CHANGELOG.md) (English) or [CHANGELOG.zh.md](./CHANGELOG.zh.md) and the [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/maxwell-feng/dsh-tinyfish-search/releases) page.
